meta.purpose: Government scheme information for farmers and students
meta.disclaimer: Simplified sample data. Amounts, limits and rules are approximate and change often. Always verify on the official website before applying.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi
schemes.summary: Direct income support to landholding farmer families, paid straight into the bank account.
benefits: Rs 6,000 per year per farmer family
Paid in 3 equal installments of Rs 2,000 every 4 months
Money goes directly to the bank account (DBT)
eligibility: Farmer family owning cultivable land
Indian citizen
Not eligible: institutional landholders, income tax payers, serving or retired government officers with high pay or pension, professionals like doctors and lawyers
documents_required: Bank account details linked with Aadhaar
how_to_apply: Visit the PM-KISAN website or the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC)
Choose 'New Farmer Registration'
Enter Aadhaar, mobile number and state, then fill land and bank details
Complete e-KYC so installments are not blocked
Track status using 'Know Your Status'
sample_questions: How can I get Rs 6000 from the government as a farmer?
Why is my PM-KISAN installment not received?

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
schemes.summary: Crop insurance that protects farmers against loss from drought, flood, pests, hailstorm and other natural causes.
benefits: Insurance cover for crop loss
Low premium for farmers: about 2% for kharif crops, 1.5% for rabi crops, 5% for commercial and horticulture crops
Remaining premium is paid by government
eligibility: Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas
Both owner farmers and tenant or sharecropper farmers
Loan farmers are often enrolled through their bank
how_to_apply: Apply before the last date of the crop season through the bank, CSC, insurance agent or the PMFBY portal
Fill crop and land details and pay the farmer share of the premium
Report crop loss within 72 hours using the crop insurance app or helpline
sample_questions: My crop was damaged by rain, what should I do?
How much premium do I pay for crop insurance?

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (through banks, supported by RBI and NABARD)
schemes.summary: Short-term credit card for farmers to buy seeds, fertilizer and other farm inputs at low interest.
benefits: Easy farm loan with revolving credit limit
Interest subvention that brings effective interest down to about 4% on timely repayment
Collateral-free loan up to a limit (about Rs 2 lakh in this estimate)
Accident insurance cover with the card
eligibility: Farmers, tenant farmers, sharecroppers and self-help groups
Also available for dairy and fisheries needs
how_to_apply: Go to your nearest bank branch or cooperative bank
Fill the KCC application form
Submit documents and wait for verification
Receive the card and use the credit limit as needed
sample_questions: How can a farmer get a cheap loan?
What is the interest rate on Kisan Credit Card?

schemes.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
schemes.summary: Free soil testing and a card telling the farmer which nutrients the soil needs.
benefits: Free soil test
Crop-wise fertilizer recommendations
Lower fertilizer cost and better yield
Card refreshed every 2 years
eligibility: All farmers with agricultural land
how_to_apply: Contact the local agriculture office or Krishi Vigyan Kendra
Give a soil sample from your field
Collect the Soil Health Card after testing or download it from the portal
sample_questions: How do I check my soil quality for free?
How much fertilizer should I use?

schemes.name: PM-KUSUM (Solar for Farmers)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
schemes.summary: Subsidy for farmers to install solar pumps and solar plants, reducing diesel and electricity cost.
benefits: Subsidy on standalone solar irrigation pumps (roughly 30% central + 30% state, farmer pays the rest)
Option to sell extra solar power to the grid for extra income
Option to solarize existing grid pumps
eligibility: Individual farmers, groups of farmers, cooperatives and panchayats
Must have suitable land for a pump or plant
how_to_apply: Apply on your state nodal agency portal or the PM-KUSUM portal
Select pump capacity and pay the farmer share
Installation is done by an approved vendor
sample_questions: How can I get a subsidised solar pump?
Can farmers earn money from solar power?

schemes.name: National Agriculture Market (eNAM)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (through SFAC)
schemes.summary: Online trading platform that connects mandis so farmers can sell produce to buyers across states at better prices.
benefits: Transparent online bidding
Better price discovery
Payment directly to the farmer's bank account
Wider market beyond the local mandi
eligibility: Farmers selling produce at an eNAM-linked mandi
Registration is free
how_to_apply: Register on the eNAM portal or app, or at your nearest eNAM mandi
Bring produce to the mandi for assaying and bidding
Receive payment in your bank account
sample_questions: Where can I sell my crop for a better price?
How do I register on eNAM?

schemes.name: PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana
schemes.summary: Pension scheme for small and marginal farmers after age 60.
benefits: Pension of Rs 3,000 per month after age 60
Family pension to spouse in case of the farmer's death (50%)
Monthly contribution depends on entry age
eligibility: Small and marginal farmers with up to 2 hectares of land
Age 18 to 40 at the time of joining
Not covered by other pension schemes like EPFO or NPS
documents_required: Bank account or Jan Dhan account
how_to_apply: Visit the nearest CSC with documents
Enroll and set up monthly auto-debit
Contribution is roughly Rs 55 to Rs 200 per month depending on age
sample_questions: Is there a pension for farmers?
How much should I pay monthly for farmer pension?

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Jal Shakti and Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
schemes.summary: Supports irrigation and water saving with drip and sprinkler systems.
benefits: Subsidy on drip and sprinkler irrigation (higher for small and marginal farmers)
Saves water and improves crop yield
Support for water source creation and watershed development
eligibility: Farmers with agricultural land
Subsidy percentage differs by state and farmer category
how_to_apply: Apply through your state horticulture or agriculture department portal
Get the system installed from an approved vendor
Subsidy is released after inspection
sample_questions: Is there a subsidy for drip irrigation?
How can I save water in my farm?

schemes.name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund
schemes.summary: Cheap loans for building cold storage, warehouses, processing units and other post-harvest infrastructure.
benefits: Loans with interest subvention of about 3% on loans up to Rs 2 crore
Credit guarantee support
Long repayment period
eligibility: Farmers, farmer producer organisations (FPOs), cooperatives, agri-entrepreneurs and start-ups
how_to_apply: Register on the AIF portal
Upload the project report and documents
Apply through a participating bank
sample_questions: I want to build a cold storage, can I get a loan?
What help is there for FPOs?

schemes.name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana
schemes.summary: Promotes organic farming through clusters of farmers.
benefits: Financial help for organic inputs, certification and marketing (about Rs 50,000 per hectare over 3 years in this estimate)
Training and support for organic farming clusters
Better price for organic produce
eligibility: Farmers willing to form a cluster of about 20 hectares or 50 farmers
Commitment to organic practices
how_to_apply: Contact the district agriculture office
Form or join an organic farming cluster
Register through the state agriculture department
sample_questions: How can I start organic farming with government help?
Is there support for organic certification?

schemes.name: National Scholarship Portal
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education (single window for many scholarships)
schemes.summary: One online portal where students can find and apply for many central and state scholarships.
benefits: Apply to many scholarships using one login
Scholarship money goes directly to the bank account
Application status tracking
eligibility: Depends on the scholarship
Usually based on class, marks, family income and category
how_to_apply: Register as a new student on the portal
Log in and fill the application form
Upload documents
Submit and get it verified by the institute

schemes.summary: Financial help for Scheduled Caste students studying after class 10.
benefits: Tuition and compulsory fee reimbursement
Maintenance allowance

eligibility: Scheduled Caste student studying after class 10
Parental income up to about Rs 2.5 lakh per year
Indian citizen
how_to_apply: Apply through the National Scholarship Portal
Submit documents
Institute and state verify the application

schemes.name: PM YASASVI Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
schemes.summary: Umbrella scheme with scholarships for OBC, EBC and DNT students from school to higher studies.
benefits: Annual scholarship amount depending on class and course
Support for good schools and for higher education
eligibility: OBC, EBC or DNT student
Family income up to about Rs 2.5 lakh per year
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal
Fill details, upload documents and submit
Get verification from the institute

schemes.name: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarships for College and University Students
schemes.ministry: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
schemes.summary: Merit-based scholarship for students who scored well in class 12 and are pursuing regular college education.
benefits: Around Rs 10,000 per year for the first 3 years of graduation (approximate amount)
Around Rs 20,000 per year in later years of postgraduation (approximate amount)
eligibility: Scored above the 80th percentile in class 12 board stream-wise
Regular college or university course
Family income up to about Rs 4.5 lakh per year
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal
Submit documents and get college verification
Renew every year with marks

benefits: Around Rs 50,000 per year (tuition fee plus allowance, demo value)
Paid for the duration of the course
eligibility: Girl student admitted to an AICTE-approved institute
Family income up to about Rs 8 lakh per year
Maximum two girls per family
how_to_apply: Apply through the National Scholarship Portal
Select the AICTE Pragati scholarship
Upload documents and submit

schemes.name: AICTE Saksham Scholarship for Specially Abled Students
schemes.summary: Scholarship for students with disabilities pursuing technical education.
benefits: Around Rs 50,000 per year (approximate amount)
Support through the whole course
eligibility: Disability of 40% or more
Admitted to an AICTE-approved institute
Family income up to about Rs 8 lakh per year
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal
Choose Saksham scholarship
Upload disability certificate and other documents

schemes.name: INSPIRE-SHE Scholarship
schemes.summary: Scholarship for talented students who choose natural or basic sciences for higher education.
benefits: Around Rs 80,000 per year in total including mentorship support (approximate amount)
Up to 5 years for BSc and MSc integrated courses
eligibility: Top performers in class 12 boards or in national entrance exams
Pursuing BSc, BS, Int. MSc in natural or basic sciences
how_to_apply: Register on the INSPIRE portal during the application window
Upload marksheet and proofs
Submit and wait for the merit list

schemes.name: PM Vidyalaxmi Education Loan Scheme
schemes.ministry: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
schemes.summary: Collateral-free education loans with interest support for students admitted to top-ranked institutions.
benefits: Collateral-free and guarantor-free loans
Interest subvention of about 3% on loans up to Rs 10 lakh for eligible families (approximate amount)
Credit guarantee support for larger loans
eligibility: Student admitted to a top-ranked higher education institution
Interest subsidy for family income up to about Rs 8 lakh and not getting other scholarships or interest benefits
how_to_apply: Register on the PM Vidyalaxmi portal
Fill the common education loan application
Choose participating banks and submit

Reward money on certification in some programmes

School or college dropouts and unemployed youth

Register with Aadhaar
Join the course and take the assessment
